summary: Parallel model shard downloads fail with 403s due to CGNAT ephemeral port collisions on customer's egress path
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403s and corrupted ranged downloads when their private deployment attempts to fetch model shards in parallel (10-20 concurrent range GETs). Failures only occur when the customer's egress path transits a carrier-grade NAT (CGNAT) device provided by their ISP.

Impact:
- Production model loads failing ~15-40% of parallel shard fetch attempts, causing increased model startup latency and occasional inference timeouts for user requests.
- Errors are presigned-url 403s and occasional HTTP range truncation requiring retry.

Environment:
- Customer: DataQube Analytics (dedicated private deploy, VPC peered to redwood control plane)
- Region: us-east
- Serving nodes: rwinf-dedicated-ssd-gpu-32 (pool of 6)
- Model: gpt-large-v2 (sharded objects, parallel range GETs)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure private deployment with VPC egress through the customer's transit provider that uses CGNAT.
2) Trigger model pull with concurrency=16 (redwood agent parallel range strategy) or run 'rwinf fetch --parallel 16 <model>'
3) Observe presigned GETs for shards: many requests return 403 or range truncation errors within 5-30s of start.
4) Reducing parallelism to 2-4 eliminates failures; routing egress via a non-CGNAT path eliminates failures at original concurrency.
observed_behavior: When multiple concurrent presigned GETs reuse ephemeral source ports due to CGNAT port preservation behavior, our upstream CDNs interpret multiplexed connections as invalid (presigned tokens bound to 5-tuple). Result: 403 responses and partial range bodies causing shard integrity failures.
expected_behavior: Parallel shard fetches succeed with presigned URLs regardless of NAT topology as long as the source IP:port uniqueness assumptions are preserved, or SDK should gracefully fall back to fewer concurrent connections when we detect 5xx/403 patterns from origin.
logs: [2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] agent: connection reuse detected - source-port collision observed by customer NAT logs (10 concurrent flows collapsed to 1 source port)
[2026-03-10T14:02:14Z] serving-runtime: shard-12 integrity check failed (sha256 mismatch) after partial download
workaround: Customer can: 1) reduce model pull parallelism to 2-4; 2) route egress via a path that does not employ CGNAT (static public IP or egress NAT with large ephemeral port pool); 3) configure agent to serialize presigned-URL fetches for this model as a temporary mitigation.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 15:00 - Support (Ava): Confirmed pattern reproducible in customer's staging with their ISP's CGNAT path.

2026-03-10 16:20 - Networking (Mateo): Captured tcpdump at agent side; src port reuse visible when >8 concurrent outbound connections are created. Client-side NAT translates multiple internal sockets to same external port leading to 5-tuple mismatch at CDN.

2026-03-10 17:10 - Storage (Priya): CDN expects presigned URL requests to come from the original client 5-tuple; when CGNAT translates multiple internal flows to same external 5-tuple, signature validation fails or origin treats as replay and returns 403.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Eng: Verified that reducing concurrency prevents collisions but does not address root cause. Consider adding origin-tolerant signature mode or agent-side per-request nonce binding.
comments: Ava Chen (Support) - 2026-03-10T15:05Z: Customer ran agent with --parallel=16 and returned 403s repeatedly. Attached NAT logs from their edge showing 1 external port mapping for multiple internal sockets.

Mateo Rivera (Networking) - 2026-03-10T16:30Z: Reproduced locally by injecting a CGNAT emulator; observed same behavior. Proposed short-term: add concurrency cap for presigned fetches in agent config. Long-term: discuss origin signature relaxation or a handshake to allow multi-stream downloads behind NAT.

Customer (DataQube) - 2026-03-10T18:02Z: We can switch to an alternate egress IP but this will require change window. Please advise best temporary setting for our deployment to restore throughput with minimal impact.
Support (Ava) - 2026-03-11T08:00Z: Recommended agent flag set: RWINF_MAX_SHARD_DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY=4 and confirmed successful model pull in customer test run.
root_cause: Customer's ISP CGNAT collapses multiple ephemeral ports into a single external source port for simultaneous connections. Presigned URLs and some CDNs validate requests based on the perceived 5-tuple and detect collisions as replay/invalid requests, returning 403s or causing partial range delivery.
resolution: Partial: Provided a supported agent config workaround (cap parallel downloads) and documented steps for customer to route egress through a non-CGNAT path. Engineering evaluating a resilient download mode in the agent that serializes or staggers presigned URL usage and retries with fresh nonces when origin 403 patterns are detected.
postmortem_follow_up:
- Implement agent-side presigned fetch backoff/stagger behavior and opt-in 'port-safe' mode for private deployments behind NATs.
- Add diagnostic probe in agent to detect CGNAT-like port preservation and surface recommendation automatically.
- Update presigned URL guidance in onboarding docs.
resolution_notes: Workaround validated by customer on 2026-03-11; customer agreed to schedule egress path change during maintenance window. Engineering ticket created to track long-term fix (INT-770310).
